- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 74+ → 75+ forecasted when true drops to 70–72).
- Model underestimates prices in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days), showing mean reversion bias — fails to anticipate downward drift after peaks.
- Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in downward trends — model reacts too slowly to falling prices.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts remain elevated when true prices are trending down, especially after 70+ peaks.
- In low-price regimes (below 65), model underestimates further, often missing sharp drops or failing to recognize bottoming-out.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility — underestimates short-term volatility spikes and overestimates stability in medium-term forecasts.
- When history shows strong downward momentum, model fails to adjust forecast downward sufficiently — often underestimates the depth of the drop.
- Model overcorrects after sharp upward moves — forecasts drop too aggressively, then rebound too early, missing true bottom.
